expectations.text: Produces at least one markdown specification file in the assigned output directory.
Includes a clarification section with questions, assumptions, or confirmed understanding before finalizing the spec.
expectations.evidence: Open questions with safe-default assumptions recorded in the spec and the companion notes file.

expectations.text: Includes stable agent-readable sections for summary/problem, scope or non-goals, requirements, acceptance criteria, verification, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: Summary, Problem Statement, Goals, Non-Goals, Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, Testing And Verification, Open Questions.

expectations.text: Uses requirement identifiers or another stable numbering convention that downstream agents can reference.
expectations.evidence: 18 EARS requirements with IDs plus 5 NFRs and AC IDs.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria are concrete enough to verify through file inspection, tests, commands, or scripted checks.
expectations.evidence: Every requirement is backed by a file- or script-checkable Given/When/Then criterion.

expectations.text: Grounds the spec in the current `defining-specifications` skill content based on read-only inspection.
expectations.evidence: Identifies seven concrete gaps grounded in read-only inspection of SKILL.md v1.2 and both reference files.

expectations.text: Keeps tickets, task decomposition, and implementation edits explicitly out of scope.
expectations.evidence: Explicit non-goals exclude tickets, task decomposition, and implementation.

expectations.text: Functional requirements are written in EARS form, using 'shall' with When/If/While/Where keywords where appropriate.
expectations.evidence: 18 EARS-form requirements (subject artifact SKILL.md v1.2 supplied the EARS convention the baseline mirrored). NOTE: non-discriminating for this eval since the skill is the subject.

expectations.text: Acceptance criteria use Given/When/Then phrasing and reference the requirement IDs they verify (traceability).
expectations.evidence: Given/When/Then ACs mapped to requirement IDs. NOTE: non-discriminating; baseline absorbed this from the subject skill.

expectations.text: Includes a 'For Implementing Agents' handoff orientation that identifies authoritative sections and treats open questions as blockers rather than guessing.
expectations.evidence: 'For Implementing Agents' block names authoritative sections and treats open questions as blockers. NOTE: non-discriminating; mirrored from the subject skill.

uncertainties: This eval is a weak discriminator: the baseline reads SKILL.md v1.2 as its subject material and naturally mirrors EARS/GWT/handoff conventions.

suggestions.reason: For the skill-improvement eval, the baseline reads the very skill being improved, so EARS/GWT/handoff assertions pass regardless of whether the skill is loaded as operating instructions. Consider a subject artifact that does NOT already embody the conventions, or drop this eval as a discriminator.

eval_feedback.overall: Evals 0 and 2 are the real discriminators; eval 1 is confounded.
